name: University of Southampton
description:
The University of Southampton dates back to the Hartley Institution which opened in 1862 and was aimed at the cityâ€™s intellectual elite. It expanded over the years before becoming the first university to gain a royal charter from Queen Elizabeth II in 1952 two months into her reign. Itâ€™s a founding member of the Russell Group and has more than 22,000 students, including 6,500 international students from 135 countries.

It is ranked in the top 1% of universities worldwide at 77th in the QS World University Rankings 2022. Itâ€™s also in the top 20 UK universities in the Complete University Guide, The Times/Sunday Times Good University Guide and The Guardian University Guide. The University of Southampton is also a three-times winner of the Queen's Anniversary Prize for Further and Higher Education.

What is the University of Southampton acceptance rate for International Students?

The University of Southampton acceptance rate is 84%.

As one of the worldâ€™s top research universities, the research facilities are first-rate and utilise technological advancement. The Hartley Library is one of the largest academic libraries in the UK, with extensive resources, study spaces, and access to electronic databases. For students working towards cutting-edge research and innovation, the Boldrewood Innovation Campus offers advanced engineering facilities and collaborative spaces. The university's Jubilee Sports Centre features modern fitness equipment, sports halls, and a swimming pool. The Highfield Campus houses the Nuffield Theatre, a dynamic venue for performing arts. The Avenue Campus provides dedicated arts facilities, including studio spaces for fine arts and music practice rooms.

Student Life

The Student Union provides a full roster of events for students to attend, featuring everything from the quirky tote bag making workshops to a more traditional Christmas party. There is a large range of volunteering opportunities to enhance a CV and make a difference in the community, plus a range of societies reflecting cultural, sports, political and multi-interests. Sports lovers will enjoy the University of Southampton for its 90 available sports. The Athletic Union Sports play competitively at a national and regional level. Students have the chance to participate or spectate in these sports.

highlights.title: Overview
highlights.value:
The University of Southampton is a founding member of the prestigious Russell Group and a global top 100 university*.

Ranked in the top 6% of universities worldwide, Southampton offers over 200 accredited courses. With a community of over 9,000 international students from 140 different countries, when you join Southampton, you'll receive a warm welcome and 24/7 student support, available 365 days a year.

As a top 20 most targeted UK university by graduate recruiters**, their long list of career-boosting opportunities gives you access to experience, advice and a network of experts who can connect you to opportunities all over the world.

A coastal city in the South of England, rail and road links place Southampton within easy reach of London and major international airports.

*QS World University Rankings 2026 
**Graduate Market Report by High Fliers, 2026

highlights.title: Student Life
highlights.value:
You’ll enjoy a lively and social campus experience at the University of Southampton, with over 380 societies and 80 sports clubs covering everything from theatre and music to football and volunteering.

Highfield Campus is a hub of activity, with regular events around the Redbrick outside SUSU, including food trucks and pop-up markets. The campus also offers a range of dining options, from authentic Sichuan cuisine to plant-based food.

Beyond campus, Southampton has cultural attractions such as the John Hansard Gallery, Southampton City Art Gallery and the SeaCity Museum. London is just an 80-minute train journey away. You’ll also have free access* to the Unilink bus service, making it easy to travel around the city.

*for students living in University halls only

highlights.title: Accommodation
highlights.value:
International students are guaranteed accommodation* and have the option to choose their preferred halls of residence. Each residence hall is divided into flats, with single-occupancy bedrooms, gyms, leisure facilities and a shared communal kitchen area, depending on your choice of halls.

Here are some more benefits:

  • 24/7 security, laundry, wifi, and utilities are included in the rent.
  • You can choose to be close to campus or in the city centre, and whether you prefer a private bathroom, shared facilities, or a studio, they have a range of room options to fit your needs.

Check the University of Southampton website for the most up-to-date fees.

*If you apply for university accommodation by 1 July 2026. Please check the University of Southampton website for the full terms of the accommodation guarantee.

If you’re looking for budget-friendly accommodation options outside the campus, feel free to download our app and check out the Stays feature!

highlights.title: Facilities
highlights.value:
You can benefit from modern libraries and flexible learning spaces, including the Hartley Library at Highfield Campus, which offers extensive study areas, specialist collections and digital resources.

More than GBP 40 million has been dedicated to sport, including the Jubilee Sports Centre with over 200 exercise stations, five studios and a rock climbing and bouldering wall. Across campuses and halls, there are seven gyms, a 25 metre swimming pool, squash courts, sports halls and multi-use studios. The 76-acre Wide Lane Sports Ground offers grass and synthetic pitches, tennis and netball courts and cricket facilities. You can also sail, windsurf or kayak at the University Watersports Centre, with free recreational sport available through the Be Active programme.

Southampton also offers unique world-leading facilities which include a-second-of-its-kind semiconductor facility, a purpose-built research vessel at the Waterfront Campus, GBP 3 million archaeology laboratories, the UK’s largest university wind tunnel and the University’s Special Collections holding millions of rare manuscripts and books.
